chunks: And by this chain, he said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying to his companions one day: 'Do not find faults with the one who comes to you with his cordiality, and do not let him remain upon the sin which he is indulging in, for it is not from the morals of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), nor is it from the morals of his friends.'

He (the narrator) said, 'And Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'The best inheritance which the fathers can leave for their children is the etiquettes (discipline) and not the wealth, for the wealth goes away whilst the discipline remains'. Mas'adat (the narrator) said, 'What is meant by the discipline is the knowledge'.

He (the narrator) said, 'Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'If there are two days left from your life, so make one of them for your manners to seek help for the day of your death'. So it was said to him (peace be upon him), 'And what is that which is the help?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Good management of what you leave behind and what you order for'.

He (the narrator) said, 'And Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) wrote to a man: 'In the Name of Allah (the Exalted) the Beneficent, the Merciful. Having said that, so the hypocrite does not like that which makes the Believers to be happy, and the happy one is he who heeds the advice of the piety, even if the advice is meant for the others'.

key_terms.السَّعِيدُ: The happy one (one who attains success)
key_terms.الْأَدَبُ: Etiquette, discipline, or good character, here specified as knowledge
key_terms.يَخْضَعُ لَهَا: Submits or yields to it (referring to a sin)

ai.seo_question: What is the best inheritance according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and how should one prepare for death?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq, 'adab' is explicitly equated with knowledge, elevating intellectual and spiritual refinement above transient material wealth as the true inheritance. The Imam advises believers to practice graciousness by not exposing the faults of those who approach with sincerity, a practice rooted in the Prophet's character, while also urging the prudent allocation of time to manage one's legacy for the day of death. The passage concludes by contrasting the hypocrite, who rejects the success of believers, with the truly happy believer who internalizes the essence of piety.
